card: This PR replaces string-based configuration argument handling in ArgsManager with compile-time type-safe declarations using a new common::Setting template class. Currently, settings are registered and queried via unchecked string literals, allowing typos, conflicting type queries, and default-value mismatches to compile without warnings. A scripted-diff commit converts setting registrations and lookups across 100 files to typed Setting::Register and Setting::Get calls. The change establishes compile-time safety and serves as the foundation for runtime type checking and validation in #16545 and #22978.
changed_since_previous: Rebased over Boost dependency cleanups (#34495/#34496), moved node constants to `src/node/settings.h` to avoid exposing Boost headers to settings consumers, added CMake include paths for UniValue/Boost/libevent to fix platform build failures, and refreshed IWYU includes in `init.cpp`.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently settings are registered and retrieved like: argsman.AddArg("-pid=<file>", ...); args.GetPathArg("-pid", BITCOIN_PID_FILENAME)... But this is not ideal because nothing checks that setting names are spelled correctly, or that default values are used consistently in the help string and retrieval sites, or that settings are retrieved with consistent types.'

PR description: 'a branch in issue #22978 extends the Setting class implemented here to support runtime setting validation, additional types like std::variant, additional conversion options, custom types, custom validation, and groups of settings declared as options structs.'
problem: Command-line and configuration settings are referenced by raw string literals without compile-time checking. Typos in argument names are not caught at compile time, retrieval sites can parse conflicting types, and default values can silently drift between user help text and code fallback logic.

risk.why: A typo or incorrect type mapping in the generated settings headers could misparse critical runtime options, wallet configurations, or RPC parameters at startup.

scope_notes: Very wide mechanical change touching 100 files (+3727/-1122). Almost all call-site changes are generated in a single scripted-diff commit via a temporary Python script (`contrib/devtools/reg-settings.py`), creating 15 new `*_settings.h` headers. A circular dependency linter rule is added to prevent `*_settings.h` headers from being included inside other headers.
summary: This pull request replaces string-based argument registration and lookup in ArgsManager with compile-time type-safe declarations using a new `common::Setting` template class. Argument name, expected type (bool, int, string, path, or list), description, and default values are centralized into static setting declarations across dedicated `*_settings.h` headers. A scripted diff migrates setting registrations and lookups repository-wide from `AddArg` and `Get*Arg` to typed `Setting::Register` and `Setting::Get` calls.
